mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital declines.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 9.5%) signals a weak labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through stronger corporate earnings and economic expansion.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST and RSAFS both above 90th percentile fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recovery phases, rising industrial production (INDPRO) reflects improving supply conditions and economic activity, yielding positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-recession recovery regime, INDPRO growth does not lead to positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market activity (HOUST) serves as a leading indicator of economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: HOUST growth fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 218.0) triggers concerns about monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in higher interest rates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 218.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent employment growth (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) signal a strengthening labor market, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated consumer confidence.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, robust retail sales (RSAFS) indicate sustained consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits rise.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, RSAFS growth does not lead to positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 50% of cases.
